name: mint-mac-care
title: Mint - Smart Disk and Memory for You and Your Agents
description: Smart disk and memory for you and your agents: space back without deleting, RAM back from idle apps, and what Codex, Claude Code and Cursor leave behind
author: dzg-studio

commands.name: mint-status
commands.title: View Mac Status
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: What Mint can get back, then disk space, memory and organized folders at a glance, with their Auto Care, like Mint's menu bar

commands.name: mint-optimize
commands.title: Optimize Storage
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Get space back without deleting anything, as Mint's Optimize does: identical copies share their storage and idle files are stored compressed, by source like Codex, Claude Code, Cursor and your files

commands.name: mint-scan
commands.title: Free Disk
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Free disk space: share identical copies, clean the caches, logs and build output apps make again, and choose from your own files

commands.name: mint-organize
commands.title: Organize a Folder
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: How many loose files each folder has to sort and where they go, then tidy it in one step

commands.name: mint-memory
commands.title: Free Memory
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Quit idle apps to free RAM in one step, or choose which apps to quit

commands.name: mint-autocare
commands.title: Auto Care
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Turn Mint's Auto Care on or off for Optimizable, Safe to clean and Yours, memory and each organized folder, as in the app

commands.name: mint-uninstall
commands.title: Uninstall App
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Find an app and what it left behind, then move them to the Trash

commands.name: mint-undo
commands.title: Undo Mint Action
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Restore eligible files from recent Mint operations while files and recovery records remain available

commands.name: mint-why
commands.title: Show Disk Growth
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: What grew on your disk this week, by app, folder, category or AI tool

commands.name: mint-trash
commands.title: Empty Trash
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: What is in the Trash, largest first; delete chosen items or all of it after confirming in Mint

commands.name: mint-conversations
commands.title: AI Conversations
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Optimize Codex conversations, remove their pictures or delete them, clear pictures from Claude Code conversations, and review pictures one by one, each confirmed in Mint

commands.name: mint-history
commands.title: Mint History
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: What Mint cleaned, freed, organized and uninstalled, newest first, by hand or by Auto Care

commands.name: mint-handling
commands.title: File Handling
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Where Mint never acts (Protect) and where it asks first (Needs Review); loosening a rule is confirmed in Mint

commands.name: mint-rules
commands.title: Cleanup Rules
commands.subtitle: Mint
commands.description: Mint's cleanup rules: what each matches and does, a preview of what it finds now, and rules made by hand, each change confirmed in Mint

tools.name: get-disk-overview
tools.title: Get Disk Overview
tools.description: How full the Mac's disk is and what Mint found at its last Scan, in four groups: Optimizable (identical copies that can share their storage and idle files that can be stored compressed in place, nothing deleted), Safe to clean (caches, build output, leftovers that apps make again and finished agent worktrees; Free Disk deletes them permanently), Yours (the person's own files and agent worktrees that still hold their work, chosen one by one) and Keep. Read-only.

tools.name: get-memory-overview
tools.title: Get Memory Overview
tools.description: How much memory is in use and which apps hold it, in Mint's piles: Idle (Mint would quit these by itself), In use and Ask first, each app sized by what quitting it gives back. Read-only.

tools.name: get-disk-growth
tools.title: Get Disk Growth
tools.description: What grew on the Mac's disk over the last days, by app or folder and by category, from the maps Mint keeps after each Scan. Read-only.

tools.name: open-mint-command
tools.title: Open Mint Command
tools.description: Open one of Mint's commands in Raycast (Free Disk, Optimize Storage, Free Memory, Organize a Folder, Uninstall App, Show Disk Growth, View Mac Status or Auto Care) so the person reviews what it would do and confirms it there. The tool itself changes nothing.

ai.instructions: Mint must be installed for these tools to answer; if a tool says it is not, pass on its words and link. The read tools never change anything. Mint never removes, quits or moves anything from an AI answer: when the person wants space or memory back, say what Mint found with its sizes, then open the matching command with open-mint-command so they review and confirm it there. Never say something was cleaned, freed or deleted. Optimizable gives space back without deleting any file; Safe to clean is what apps make again plus finished agent worktrees (merged, nothing only there, untouched for a day), and Free Disk deletes it permanently; Yours is the person's own files and agent worktrees that still hold their work. Write sizes exactly as the tools give them.

evals.input: @mint what's taking up space on my Mac?
@mint how much space can I get back without deleting anything?
@mint which apps are using the most memory right now?
@mint what grew on my disk this week?

mocks.open-mint-command: Opened Free Disk. Nothing has changed yet: the person reviews it there and confirms.

scripts.validate: npm run lint && tsc --noEmit && npm test && npm run build
scripts.prepublishOnly: echo 'Publish this extension through the Raycast Store, not npm.' && exit 1
